transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more, because it's probably just a silly little quirk of mine, really. 

But... well, I guess what brings me in is that whenever I step into a slow elevator, or, you know, a small locked room, my chest just jumps right away. I get this... this really strong need to get back out before I can even think straight. 

It's not a huge deal, I manage alright most days, but I know it sounds a bit foolish for a man my age to get spooked like that. Does that... does that make sense to you? Am I in the right place for something like that?
When you get into an elevator or a small room, does the feeling you get resemble a panic attack—like your heart races, you feel dizzy, or you think something terrible is going to happen?

Oh, heavens no, Doctor. Nothing quite so dramatic as all that. I, uh, I wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or having a real... what did you call it, a panic attack. No, my heart doesn't go racing off, and I don't get dizzy or anything like that. And I certainly don't think anything terrible is going to happen to me. 

It's really just... well, just a strong urge to step back out into the hallway. I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, since it's not nearly as severe as what you're describing. I just like to be out in the open, I suppose. Is that... is that helpful for you to know?
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid using elevators or small rooms, and if so, does that avoidance cause you any real problems in your daily life?

Well, I... I suppose I do work around it a little bit, but please don't think it's a big burden or anything. It's really no trouble at all. I mean, these days I just take the stairs instead of the elevator. At my age, it's just good exercise, right? Keeps the old joints moving. 

And, well, I help out at the local museum, and sometimes I just pass on the archive jobs down in the small storage rooms. I just let the others handle that sort of thing. If I absolutely can't avoid a closed-in place, I might just... well, I might ask a friend to wait nearby for me. 

I know it makes me look a bit foolish, an old man asking a buddy to stand watch, but it just helps me feel more settled. It certainly doesn't cause any real problems in my day-to-day life, though, I promise. I hope that's alright? I mean, is it okay that I just sort of manage it that way?

Do you ever feel this urge to step away or avoid other kinds of situations—like being outside alone, standing in line, or being in crowded places—or is it only when you're in small, enclosed spaces like elevators or rooms?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that at all, Doctor. I'm perfectly fine outside, and I don't mind a crowd or standing in line one bit. I wouldn't want you to think I'm afraid of the whole world, you know? 

It's... it's really just those little, closed-off spots. The elevators, the little storage closets... just those. Everything else is completely fine. I'm quite normal when it comes to being out and about, I promise. Does that... does that help narrow things down for you? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
